content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU memory pressure in pool `dedicated-west-1-gpu-pool-7` — 95% memory util (threshold 90%). PagerDuty incident PD-INC-8249 created. See https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-8249

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-INC-8249 - triggered on `gpu-mem-pressure` alert rule. Escalation: primary on-call "maya" notified.

maya: acked. I'm on it — pulling logs now.

maya: quick status: dashboards showing sustained CUDA alloc failures on nodes gpu-12 and gpu-15, evictions increasing. KV cache explosions on long-running chat jobs.

alex: copying logs below — lots of `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` from runtime: 
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] model-server(gpu-12): ERROR runtime: CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED: out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] kvcache: warn: prefetched entries xfer spike -> mem pressure
[2026-03-14T09:12:07Z] model-server(gpu-12): WARNING: fallback to cpu disabled for this pool
```

kevin: looks like a combination of long KV cache lifetimes + a sudden traffic spike for chat-prod v3. We saw similar last month but not this wide.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) drain problematic nodes from pool and restart workers, 2) bump kvcache eviction threshold to 0.5GiB per-session, 3) enable fallback routing to cheaper model-variant for same route for next 10m.

maya: running drain command on gpu-12 and gpu-15 now:
```bash
# drain nodes -- graceful
redwood infra node drain --pool dedicated-west-1-gpu-pool-7 --node gpu-12 --timeout 120
redwood infra node drain --pool dedicated-west-1-gpu-pool-7 --node gpu-15 --timeout 120
```

infra-bot: drain job started for gpu-12 (job id drain-8732), gpu-15 (drain-8733). Estimated time 2m per node.

maya: bumping kvcache eviction param: `kvcache.eviction.max_per_session=536870912` (was 1073741824) to force more aggressive TTLs. Applying to pool config.

alex: also enabling model fallback for route `/chat/prod/v3` to `gpt-like-quantized-v2` for requests > 8k tokens. Command: 
```bash
redwood routes update --route /chat/prod/v3 --fallback gpt-like-quantized-v2 --limit 8000 --window 600
```

sophie: I'm monitoring customer-facing dashboards — 503 spikes up to 2.7% for the last 4m, median latency on affected routes increased from 120ms -> 420ms for some requests. No SLO breach yet but trending.

pagerduty: PD-INC-8249: acknowledged by maya at 2026-03-14T09:14:10Z.

kevin: after drains we should autoscale pool by +2 nodes (warm) to reduce allocation pressure if traffic persists. Requesting low-risk scale-up.

maya: scaling up pool +2 warm nodes now: `redwood infra pool scale --pool dedicated-west-1-gpu-pool-7 --delta +2 --mode warm`

infra-bot: pool scale job started (scale-5591). Expected add time ~90s per node.

maya: node drains finished. Restarted model-server on gpu-12 and gpu-15, memory graphs show drop in per-node allocs.

alex: logs show `kvcache evictions` spiked immediately after config change, and CUDA alloc failures dropped to single-digit occurrences.

sophie: customer impact update: 503s peaked at ~2.7% and dropped to 0.4% in the last 3 minutes. Latency on fallback model acceptable, quality checks running. No high-value customer reported major failures so far.

maya: marking incident mitigation in PD ticket. Will keep routing fallback active for 10 more minutes and then roll back if stable. Opening follow-up: postmortem + action items (kvcache autosizing, enable soft-fallback by default for heavy routes).

kevin: +1 for postmortem. Also propose adding a knob to preemptively trim kvcache per-session after X alloc spikes.

alex: note: need a playbook update to allow automatic fallback to quantized variants for dedicated pools when alloc > 85% across 2+ nodes.

pagerduty: PD-INC-8249: resolved by maya at 2026-03-14T09:22:30Z (mitigation: drains + kvcache eviction bump + pool scale + enabled fallback).

maya: resolving thread here. Summary for follow-up: 1) short-term - keep fallback enabled for 10m then rollback if stable; 2) medium - add autosize/TTL tuning for kvcache and conservative default for dedicated pools; 3) long - consider admission control to reject >N token prefetched sessions. I'll own the postmortem and tag SRE + runtime teams.

sophie: noted. I'll message support to flag customers that might see quality changes from fallback and prepare comms if needed.

kevin: thanks all.

maya: thanks — closing thread.
